countries.subject: Kenya
countries.name: Kenya
countries.content: Kenya is a country. Capital: Nairobi. East Africa. Swahili and English. Currency KES. Known for wildlife and the Great Rift Valley.

countries.subject: Nigeria
countries.name: Nigeria
countries.content: Nigeria is a country. Capital: Abuja. West Africa. Most populous African country. Currency Naira. Lagos is a major commercial city.

countries.subject: South Africa
countries.name: South Africa
countries.content: South Africa is a country. Capital: Pretoria. Three capitals including Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Rainbow Nation.

countries.subject: Egypt
countries.name: Egypt
countries.content: Egypt is a country. Capital: Cairo. Nile River. Ancient civilization and pyramids. Currency EGP.

countries.subject: Ghana
countries.name: Ghana
countries.content: Ghana is a country. Capital: Accra. West Africa. Cocoa and gold. Currency Cedi.

countries.subject: Ethiopia
countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.content: Ethiopia is a country. Capital: Addis Ababa. African Union headquarters. Never fully colonized.

countries.subject: Tanzania
countries.name: Tanzania
countries.content: Tanzania is a country. Capital: Dodoma. Kilimanjaro and Serengeti. Zanzibar islands.

countries.subject: Uganda
countries.name: Uganda
countries.content: Uganda is a country. Capital: Kampala. Lake Victoria region. Source of the Nile related geography.

countries.subject: Rwanda
countries.name: Rwanda
countries.content: Rwanda is a country. Capital: Kigali. East Africa. Known for post-1994 recovery and technology push.

countries.subject: United States
countries.name: United States
countries.content: United States is a country. Capital: Washington DC. 50 states. Major tech and research universities.

countries.subject: United Kingdom
countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.content: United Kingdom is a country. Capital: London. Constitutional monarchy. English language and common law influence.

countries.subject: France
countries.name: France
countries.content: France is a country. Capital: Paris. European Union member. Known for science culture and engineering.

countries.subject: Germany
countries.name: Germany
countries.content: Germany is a country. Capital: Berlin. Largest EU economy by many measures. Strong engineering tradition.

countries.subject: China
countries.name: China
countries.content: China is a country. Capital: Beijing. Most populous country. Manufacturing and technology hub.

countries.subject: India
countries.name: India
countries.content: India is a country. Capital: New Delhi. Large democracy. Major IT and education sector.

countries.subject: Japan
countries.name: Japan
countries.content: Japan is a country. Capital: Tokyo. Advanced technology and robotics. Island nation in East Asia.

countries.subject: Australia
countries.name: Australia
countries.content: Australia is a country. Capital: Canberra. Island continent. Strong universities and research.

countries.subject: Brazil
countries.name: Brazil
countries.content: Brazil is a country. Capital: Brasilia. Amazon rainforest. Portuguese-speaking South America.

countries.subject: Canada
countries.name: Canada
countries.content: Canada is a country. Capital: Ottawa. Bilingual English French. Natural resources and research.

countries.subject: Russia
countries.name: Russia
countries.content: Russia is a country. Capital: Moscow. Largest country by area. Spans Europe and Asia.

science.subject: BODMAS
science.content: BODMAS is the order of operations used in many school systems including Kenya: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

science.subject: Photosynthesis
science.content: Plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen using sunlight and chlorophyll.

science.subject: Water cycle
science.content: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection move water through Earth's systems.

science.subject: Gravity
science.content: Gravity is the attraction between masses. On Earth, gravitational acceleration is about 9.8 m/s².

science.subject: Atom
science.content: An atom has a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it. Atomic number equals proton count.

science.subject: Neutron
science.content: A neutron is an uncharged particle in the atomic nucleus, slightly heavier than a proton.

science.subject: Neurotransmitter
science.content: Chemical messengers at synapses such as dopamine, serotonin, acetylcholine, GABA and glutamate.

science.subject: DNA
science.content: DNA carries genetic information as a double helix of nucleotide bases A T C G.

science.subject: pH
science.content: pH measures acidity: 7 neutral, below 7 acidic, above 7 alkaline.

science.subject: Speed of light
science.content: In vacuum, light travels at about 299,792 km/s.

science.subject: Force
science.content: Newton's second law: F = ma (force equals mass times acceleration).

science.subject: Energy
science.content: Energy is the capacity to do work. Forms include kinetic, potential, thermal, chemical, electrical.

science.subject: Cell
science.content: The cell is the basic unit of life. Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus; eukaryotic cells have one.

science.subject: Evolution
science.content: In biology, evolution is change in heritable traits of populations over generations, explained mainly by natural selection and other mechanisms.

science.subject: Climate vs weather
science.content: Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions; climate is the long-term average pattern.

science.subject: Synapse
science.content: The junction where neurons communicate, often by releasing neurotransmitters.

science.subject: Action potential
science.content: A rapid electrical signal that travels along a neuron's axon when the cell fires.

technology.subject: HTML
technology.content: HTML structures web pages with elements such as headings, paragraphs, links, and forms.

technology.subject: CSS
technology.content: CSS styles HTML: layout, colors, fonts, and responsive design.

technology.subject: JavaScript
technology.content: JavaScript adds interactivity in browsers and can also run on servers (Node.js).

technology.subject: HTTP
technology.content: HTTP is the protocol for web requests. HTTPS adds encryption with TLS.

technology.subject: API
technology.content: An API lets programs communicate, often using JSON over HTTP.

technology.subject: SQL
technology.content: SQL queries relational databases: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, JOIN.

technology.subject: Git
technology.content: Git tracks versions of code: commit, branch, merge, push, pull.

technology.subject: Algorithm
technology.content: An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps to solve a problem or compute a result.

technology.subject: Data structure
technology.content: Common structures: arrays, lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, graphs.

technology.subject: Machine learning
technology.content: ML learns patterns from data: supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.

technology.subject: Neural network
technology.content: A neural network is a layered model of connected nodes trained by adjusting weights.

technology.subject: Microprocessor
technology.content: A microprocessor is an IC that implements a CPU: fetch, decode, and execute instructions.

technology.subject: Optical transceiver
technology.content: Converts electrical signals to light and back for fiber links (SFP, QSFP, etc.).

technology.subject: Cloud computing
technology.content: On-demand computing resources over the internet: servers, storage, databases, services.

technology.subject: Cybersecurity basics
technology.content: Protect systems with strong passwords, updates, encryption, least privilege, and awareness of phishing.

technology.subject: Nanometer
technology.content: One nanometre is 10^-9 metres — the scale of molecules and advanced chip features.

technology.subject: CAD
technology.content: Computer-aided design software for precise engineering and architectural models.

space.subject: Solar system
space.content: The Sun and planets Mercury Venus Earth Mars Jupiter Saturn Uranus Neptune; Pluto is a dwarf planet.

space.subject: Earth
space.content: Third planet from the Sun; about 71% surface water; one natural satellite, the Moon.

space.subject: Moon
space.content: Earth's Moon causes tides and shows phases; first crewed landing was in 1969.

space.subject: Galaxy
space.content: A galaxy is a large system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter. Earth is in the Milky Way.

space.subject: Black hole
space.content: A region where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.

space.subject: Big Bang
space.content: Leading scientific model for the early universe about 13.8 billion years ago.

space.subject: Satellite
space.content: An object orbiting a planet; artificial satellites support GPS, weather, and communications.

study.subject: Essay structure
study.content: Typical essay: introduction with thesis, body paragraphs with evidence, conclusion that synthesizes.

study.subject: Citation
study.content: Always credit sources. Common styles: APA, MLA, Chicago. Avoid plagiarism.

study.subject: Study method
study.content: Active recall and spaced repetition beat passive rereading for long-term memory.

study.subject: Critical thinking
study.content: Question claims, check evidence, consider alternatives, and watch for logical fallacies.

study.subject: University research
study.content: Start with a clear question, search scholarly sources, take notes, outline, draft, revise, cite.

study.subject: Time management
study.content: Break tasks into blocks, set deadlines, avoid multitasking on deep work, review weekly.

materials.subject: Iron
materials.content: Metal Fe used in steel; rusts when oxidized.

materials.subject: Copper
materials.content: Conductive metal used in electrical wiring.

materials.subject: Aluminium
materials.content: Light corrosion-resistant metal used in aircraft and packaging.

materials.subject: Loam
materials.content: Balanced soil of sand, silt, and clay; good for agriculture.

materials.subject: Clay soil
materials.content: Fine particles; holds water; can drain poorly.

materials.subject: Sandy soil
materials.content: Coarse particles; drains quickly; lower nutrient retention.

materials.subject: Air composition
materials.content: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, argon and trace gases including CO2.

materials.subject: Concrete
materials.content: Mixture of cement, aggregate, and water that hardens into a structural material.
